# Core Mechanics

A compact reminder of the V20-style rules this chronicle uses. Written for the Storyteller's quick reference, not as a rulebook.

## Dice Basics

- Roll a pool of ten-sided dice equal to an Attribute plus an Ability (or a Discipline rating). Each die that meets or beats the difficulty is a success. The default difficulty is 6.
- Each die showing 1 cancels one success. If no successes remain and at least one die shows a 1, the roll is a Botch: something goes actively wrong, not merely nothing.
- Zero successes without a 1 showing is a plain failure.
- With a relevant specialty, each 10 counts as two successes.
- A point of Willpower may be spent before a roll for one automatic success that cannot be cancelled. A roll with a Willpower success can never Botch.
- One success is a marginal result, three is a solid one, five is exceptional.

## Difficulty Ladder

| Difficulty | Feel |
|---|---|
| 3 | Trivial |
| 5 | Easy |
| 6 | Standard |
| 7 | Challenging |
| 8 | Difficult |
| 9 | Extremely difficult |

Difficulty never drops below 3 or rises above 10 in this chronicle.

## Blood and Willpower

Blood pool is capped by generation (a 13th generation vampire holds 10, a 7th holds 20). Spending a blood point heals a level of normal damage, raises a Physical Attribute for a scene, or powers a Discipline. Willpower refreshes at the Storyteller's discretion, usually once a session or when a character acts on their Nature.

## Humanity

Humanity runs from 10 down to 0. Whenever a character acts against their Humanity rating, roll Conscience against difficulty 8; failure costs a point. Humanity also caps how long a vampire can stay awake after sunrise and how convincingly they can pass for living.
